questions.question: Under anaerobic metabolism which of the following substrates yields 3 molecules of ATP?
questions.explanation: Breakdown of glycogen under anaerobic conditions yields 3 ATPs. Breakdown of glycogen yields glucose-6-phosphate which can enter the glycolysis pathway. Since it bypasses the first step, one ATP is saved and anaerobic glycolysis yields 3 ATPs. The first step in glycolysis involves conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate and requires one ATP. Glycogen breakdown leads directly to glucose-6-phosphate, thereby bypassing this ATP-requiring step. One ATP is used for conversion of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. Net ATP formed from anaerobic glycolysis of glycogen is therefore 3 ATP.

questions.question: Which of the following glycogen storage diseases is also a lysosomal storage disorder?
questions.explanation: Pompe's disease is the glycogen storage disease (GSD) that is also a lysosomal storage disorder. A small amount of glycogen is degraded by the lysosomal enzyme α(1→4)-glucosidase, also known as acid maltase. Deficiency of this enzyme causes accumulation of glycogen in vacuoles in lysosomes and is called type II GSD or Pompe's disease. The source also notes associations of glycogen storage disorders with liver cirrhosis (Types III, IV, IX), renal dysfunction (Type I), and neurologic involvement (Type II), and notes Danon disease (Type IIb) as another lysosomal glycogen storage disorder.

questions.question: After evaluation, a child with severe hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and hyperuricemia is diagnosed with von Gierke's disease. What is the inheritance pattern of this disease?
questions.explanation: Von Gierke’s disease is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Von Gierke disease (type I glycogen storage disorder) occurs due to the deficiency of glucose-6-phosphatase enzyme in the liver, kidney, and intestinal mucosa. Patients present commonly by 3-4 months of age with hypoglycemia (leading to seizures), lactic acidosis, and hepatomegaly. Affected children often have a doll-like face with fat cheeks, relatively thin extremities, short stature, and a protuberant abdomen due to massive hepatomegaly. The kidneys are also enlarged, whereas the spleen and heart are not involved. Laboratory findings include hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, and hyperlipidemia.
